_readme: Failures the editor swallows on purpose, one entry per accepted line.
Written for pdfluent-internal#413. A silent failure is the one bug class the
test suite cannot see: the code runs, returns, and the person in front of the
app gets a spinner that stopped. Some swallowing is right -- a localStorage
write that fails in a sandboxed webview must not take the document with it --
so the rule is not 'never swallow', it is that swallowing is a decision and
the decision is written down where a reviewer can disagree with it.
scripts/quality/no-silent-failures.mjs --check fails on a hit that is not
here, on an entry that matches no line any more, on an entry covering a
different number of lines than when it was written, and on an entry without a
reason. Entries are anchored on (file, kind, code) -- the trimmed source line,
not a line number -- so moving code does not invalidate them but rewriting the
line does, which is the point: rewriting the catch means re-deciding.
The counts are the measure, and they are meant to go down.
Since 2026-09-08 the list also carries skipped tests: a test that does not run is a pass nobody earned, and the UI register used to accept one as proof.

accepted.reason: startup watchdog recovery: if the main thread cannot be reached the app is already past saving, and the watchdog's next tick retries.
window management during watchdog recovery; a window that refuses to show is reported by the recovery attempt counter in the log, not by this call.
focus is cosmetic. Failing to raise a window must not abort the recovery that just created it.
closing the frozen window during recovery; the new window is already up, and a failed close leaves a stale window rather than a broken app.
opening the crash log in the platform file manager. The path is printed in the same dialog, so the user can reach it either way.
menu item opening the website in the default browser. A browser that will not launch is visible to the user immediately -- nothing happened.
stopping the text-to-speech subprocess. It is already being replaced or the app is quitting; a kill that fails leaves a process the OS reaps.
reaping the text-to-speech subprocess after kill, to avoid a zombie. There is no outcome for the user in either branch.
platform stub: binds the unused parameter on the platforms where text-to-speech is not implemented, right above the Err that tells the user so.
the security-scoped bookmark store. A corrupt store reads as empty, which drops Recent-file access rather than the file itself; the reopen then asks for the file through the normal dialog.
creating the bookmark store directory; the write on the next line is the operation that matters and it carries its own guard.
persisting security-scoped bookmarks. Losing them costs Recent-file access after a relaunch, never the open document.
debug_assertions-only bookmark self-test driven from the command line; an empty path is a valid case the self-test reports on. Not compiled into a release build.
writing to the app log itself. Logging is what runs when something has already gone wrong, so it must not become the next thing that goes wrong.
menu item opening the feedback page in the default browser; a browser that will not launch is visible to the user as nothing happening.
menu item opening the licence page in the default browser; same as the other two menu links.
forwarding a menu click to the webview. If the webview is gone the menu is gone with it; the startup watchdog owns that case.
raising the main window from the dock/taskbar handler. Cosmetic, and the user retries by clicking again.
focusing the main window from the dock/taskbar handler; cosmetic in the same way as the show above it.
delivering an open-file event to the webview. The path is also kept in take_pending_open, which the frontend polls at startup, so a dropped event is recovered.
binds the otherwise-unused run-event parameter on the platforms without an open-file event. No runtime behaviour; app_handle left the binding when the clean-quit record started using it.
removing the temporary image handed to the OCR bridge. A leftover temp file is the OS's problem; the OCR result has already been read or already failed with its own message.

optional PDF dictionary entries -- attachment /Desc, /CreationDate, and the optional-content /ON, /OFF and /Locked arrays. Absent is a legal document, and an empty value is the correct reading of it, not a swallowed error.
cleaning up the temporary export the PDF/A guard just inspected. The guard's verdict is the result; the temp file is scratch.
creating the crash-report directory; the write below it is what matters and telemetry is opt-in and off by default.
appending to the crash-report queue. A crash reporter that fails loudly during a crash makes the crash worse and tells the user nothing they can use.
deleting a crash report that has been sent. A leftover would be re-sent once; a hard failure here would block the quit path.
thumbnail generation in the retired V1 shell (?legacy). One page that will not render leaves a gap in a strip; the shipped v3 shell has its own thumbnails.
auto-sending an opt-in crash report. Telling a user that the report about the crash also failed adds a second dialog to a moment that already has one.

accepted.code: .catch(() => undefined); // command may not exist yet / no backend
accepted.reason: polling the backend for a pending Rust crash. Runs outside Tauri too, where the command does not exist; a missing crash report is the normal case.
retired V1 shell (?legacy): a user-agent probe that answers false, and an iframe fragment write that is a scroll position. Neither is reachable from the shipped shell.
retired V1 shell (?legacy); the handler writes the failure to the debug log that shell shows.
retired V1 shell (?legacy); the handler drops a stale render request and leaves the previous page on screen.
header scan for a document fingerprint. It reads the first bytes to guess XFA and page count before the real parse; the parse itself reports.
reading the OS locale. No navigator means fall through to English, which is what the user gets anyway.
reading the stored language choice. Unavailable storage falls through to the OS locale.
persisting the language choice. The switch has already taken effect; only surviving a restart is at risk.
reading the audit log out of storage. Corrupt or absent reads as empty, and the log is a record of what happened, not a thing to act on.
serialising a value into the debug log, and reading the log back. A value that will not serialise is replaced by its String() form; a corrupt log reads as empty.
parsing enterprise policy JSON. A malformed policy falls back to defaults, which is the safe direction: defaults are the most restrictive set.
decodeURI on a dropped file path. A path that will not decode is used as-is, which is right for a path that was never percent-encoded.

the pdf-lib helper module: an unknown font name falls back to Helvetica, a missing attachment is a no-op, and a signature-field probe answers with an empty report. Not on the desktop write path, which goes through the Rust engine.
a crash listener that throws must not escalate a crash into a second crash. The remaining listeners still run.
locale detection for a crash report and the report build itself. A crash report with a missing locale is still a usable crash report.
reading the id out of the 202 response. The report has been accepted at this point; the id is only used for a follow-up the user never sees.
the liveness ping to the Rust startup watchdog. Outside Tauri there is no IPC at all, and inside it a missed ping is exactly what the watchdog is for.
native text-to-speech pause/resume/stop. The bridge has already reported the command failure; this catch then falls through to the Web Speech path, which may well be the one speaking.
reading the stored reviewer identity. Absent or corrupt means the app asks for a name instead of guessing one.
persisting the reviewer identity. The name is already in use for this session; only remembering it next time is at risk.
reading computed style off a selection to seed the format controls. A failed read leaves the controls at their defaults.
reading which nav panel was open. Falls back to closed, which is the default state anyway.
persisting which nav panel is open. A layout preference, not document state.
page deletion in the organise grid. The line above sets the task-queue entry to error with a label the user reads, and the bridge has already reported the command.
sampling a pixel to pick the page background colour. Out-of-bounds means the sample is skipped and the next one is used.
copying selected text. A clipboard the browser refuses is visible the moment the user pastes, and a toast about it would fire on every denied permission prompt.

encrypt, decrypt, watermark and the three redaction actions, each of which sets its own task-queue entry to error with a label. The panel is also dead code: nothing imports it (see docs/ui_register_exceptions.json).
verifying signatures on open; an unsigned or unreadable document shows an empty signature list, which is what it has. The bridge reports the command failure.
signing from the dead signature panel; the task-queue entry above it is set to error with a label.
clipboard read during paste, with document.execCommand('paste') as the fallback on the next line -- an actual second attempt, not a shrug.
restoring the last page position for a reopened file. A failed read opens page one.
page labels. A document without them falls back to page numbers, which is what most documents use.

accepted.code: } catch { /* silent — task queue surfaces errors */ }
accepted.reason: creating shape, ink and text-markup annotations. The bridge reports the command failure to the error stack; the annotation simply does not appear.
creating and applying redactions and reordering pages. The bridge reports the command failure; the page state on screen is refetched from the document either way.
search-and-redact and delete-page both answer null on failure, and the caller renders that as no matches / no change. The bridge has already reported why.
metadata redaction answers false, which the caller turns into a failed task-queue entry. The bridge has already reported why.

accepted.code: } catch { /* silent — task queue lives in TopBar, not here */ }
accepted.reason: save-as. The bridge reports the failed save_pdf and the document stays marked dirty, so nothing is lost or claimed saved.

accepted.code: } catch { /* save failed — proceed anyway; task bar will surface the error */ }
accepted.reason: the save inside a close/reopen flow. The bridge reports it and the dirty flag is not cleared, so the unsaved-changes prompt still stands.

accepted.code: } catch { /* silent — TopBar task queue surfaces errors */ }
accepted.reason: auto-save after a form-field write. The bridge reports the failed save_pdf and the document stays dirty.
loading the AcroForm model. A document with no form presents an empty model, which is the same shape as a document whose model failed to load; the bridge reports the difference.
remembering the page you were on per file. A convenience across sessions, capped at 50 entries.
reading the recent-files list. Corrupt or absent reads as empty, and the list rebuilds as files are opened.

accepted.code: } catch { /* ignore write errors (e.g. private browsing quota) */ }
accepted.reason: persisting the recent-files list after an open.
persisting the recent-files list after a removal or a clear. The in-memory list is already updated.
createImageBitmap for the render cache. Returning null falls back to drawing the ImageData directly, so the page still paints.
reading whether the left rail was open. Falls back to open, the default.
reading the recent-commands list for the palette. Falls back to empty.
persisting the rail state and the palette's recent commands. Layout preferences.
Range.setEnd on a DOM range that has moved under the caret. Returning null means the caret offset is not derived this frame, and the next keystroke recomputes it.
reading the stored zoom level; falls back to 150%.
persisting the zoom level. The zoom has already been applied.
parsing an imported review bundle. The catch returns a typed failure with a message the import dialog shows -- the reason does reach the user, just not through this binding.
PerformanceObserver for long tasks, which WebKit does not implement. No observer means no long-task numbers, which is a gap in a diagnostic, not in the product.
reading app settings. Corrupt settings fall back to defaults rather than blocking startup on a JSON error.
persisting app settings. The setting is already in effect for this session.
recording where the autosave went. Losing the record costs the recovery prompt, not the autosaved file.
reading the recovery record. Absent or corrupt means no recovery prompt is offered, which is the same as having nothing to recover.
clearing the recovery record once the document is saved. A leftover record offers a recovery the user can decline.

accepted.code: } catch { /* keep going without a bookmark */ }
accepted.reason: minting a macOS security-scoped bookmark. Without one the file still opens now; only reopening it from Recent after a relaunch is affected, and that path asks for the file again.
resolving a stored bookmark before a Recent open. False sends the caller down the normal open-dialog path, which is the honest outcome.
releasing security-scoped access. Releasing something that was never held is the normal case, not an error.
URL parsing while scanning page text for links. Text that is not a URL is the overwhelmingly common case; null means no link is drawn.
reading whether the thumbnail drawer was open; falls back to open.
persisting the thumbnail drawer state. A layout preference.

encrypt, decrypt, metadata and watermark each set their task-queue entry to error with a label the user reads, on top of what the bridge reports. The fifth is the confirm dialog for applying redactions, which defaults to not confirmed -- a failure there cannot make a destructive action run.
reading the stored reviewer name for new comments. Empty means the app asks.

persisting the reviewer name, reading the auto-open-links preference, and setting the window title. The first two are conveniences; a window title that will not set is cosmetic and must never take the document with it.
the handler sets a hint the user reads: quit and reopen by hand. Flagged because the binding is unused, not because the failure is hidden.
the handler sets the update-check notice to failed, which the topbar renders. Flagged for the unused binding, not for hiding anything.
persisting the auto-open-external-links choice. The choice holds for this session either way.
link annotations for the current page. No links is a normal document state and the page still renders; the bridge reports the command failure.
page labels, optional in every PDF. Without them the app numbers pages; the bridge has already reported the command failure.
the attachment list. Most documents have none, so an empty list is indistinguishable from the normal case; the bridge reports the failure.
the optional-content layer list. Most documents have no layers; the bridge reports the command failure.

accepted.code: const pending = await invoke<string | null>('take_pending_open').catch(() => null);
accepted.reason: asking the backend whether a file was double-clicked to launch the app. Null means it was not, which is the usual case.

the wall clock read for a log timestamp. A clock before the Unix epoch gives a zero stamp; refusing to log the line instead would lose the message the stamp was for.

OnceLock::set fails only when the clock was already started, which is exactly the outcome wanted: the first call wins so a second run() cannot move the origin under a session that is already being measured.
